mechanism_claims.claim_text: FV-LL and the other tested peptides permeabilized the E. coli UB1005 outer membrane in the NPN uptake assay, with FV-LL strongest among the designed hybrids at low concentration.
direct_assay_types: NPN uptake outer membrane permeability assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Qualitative mechanism strength retained; exact fluorescence values were figure-only and not converted into numeric records.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: At 1x MIC, peptides increased inner membrane permeability in the ONPG assay; FV-LL was the strongest designed hybrid while ME26 was highest overall.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Ranks are source text-supported; no unsupported numeric trace was fabricated from the plotted figure.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM and TEM showed membrane surface damage and ultrastructural disruption after hybrid-peptide treatment at 1x MIC for E. coli ATCC 25922 and S. aureus ATCC 29213.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphological endpoint supports membrane disruption; it does not identify a single molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: FV-LL reduced P. aeruginosa PAO1 biofilm viability more strongly than FV7 over the tested concentration range.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm inhibition is retained as phenotype/context, not promoted to a direct molecular mechanism.
